item.title: Scammers working overtime locally and in the state Capitol
item.description: It’s unfortunate that there are so many scam artists in the world, and that includes some lawmakers in the state Capitol.

item.title: DUI, auto theft and warrant arrests keep police busy
item.description: A look at the arrest highlights from Ceres Police covering the period of March 17-23, 2026.

item.title: With literacy policies on the books, advocates target early math
item.description: Buoyed by their successful strategies for early literacy, California legislators and advocacy groups are calling for a parallel approach to math.

item.title: Costa Fields trees won’t be cut down after all
item.description: The Ceres City Council has dismissed the idea of cutting down the mature trees around the Costa Fields ball park in Smyrna Park as the city’s remedy to fixing lighting issues after installation of a new lighting system.

item.title: ACE Hardware store opens once again
item.description: Mark Yamayoshi has made a sizeable investment in reopening the Ace Hardware store in Ceres and he’s hoping to see customers return to support the business.

item.title: Ceres Rotarians honor two standout students
item.description: Two local students were honored as standouts at Friday’s Ceres Rotary Club meeting at the Ceres Community Center.

item.title: County to cut vacant, unfunded positions due to slowdown
item.description: Stanislaus County will cut nearly 150 allocated local government positions from its budget after the Board of Supervisors voted to approve the midyear report of the budget that was OK’d last September.

item.title: Will CUSD remove Chavez’s name from junior high school?
item.description: Will Ceres Unified School District be renaming Cesar Chavez Junior High School as others are removing his name in light of Dolores Huerta’s revelation that the late farm labor union founder sexually assaulted and impregnated her twice?

item.title: Dunford resigning as city manager because of family medical emergency
item.description: Doug Dunford announced on Monday that he is stepping down as Ceres city manager due to a family medical emergency.

item.title: Crowd protests city’s treatment of Ceres Youth Baseball
item.description: A large and vocal crowd of Ceres Youth Baseball officials, coaches, players and their supporters turned out at Monday’s Ceres City Council meeting to protest the city’s attempt to force changes to its contract with CYB.
